name: Coconut candy
summary: Kẹo dừa is a soft candy of coconut milk and sugar, warm at the kiln or wrapped to take home. Another account sweetens the plain piece with maltose and yellow cane sugar, and later pieces take durian, peanut, cacao, or pandan.
origin: Ben Tre. The rural page shows the boil, the cut, and the wrap at Cồn Phụng. The wrapping table shown is on Cồn Quy.
culture: Vietnam Tourism says more than 300 coconut-candy factories. The provincial tourism site, 25 November 2024, says more than 180 workshops and tens of thousands of tons a year. Both counts stand. The national rural page shows the work at Cồn Phụng and does not give a count.

The same site says elders place the craft in the 1930s, starting in Mỏ Cày, now Mỏ Cày Nam, under the old name kẹo Mỏ Cày. The plain piece on Vietnam Tourism is coconut milk and sugar. The site’s plain piece is coconut milk, maltose from sprouted glutinous rice, and yellow cane sugar.
Candy, milk, oil, and shell craft are the products of the palms. The rural page says more than 500 coconut-shell objects. That count is not a candy count.
texture: Vietnam Tourism calls the candy soft and sticky. The provincial tourism site, 25 November 2024, calls the piece chewy, sweet, and not harsh. Eat it warm at the kiln, or carry the wrapped pieces.
taste: Vietnam Tourism calls the plain piece coconut milk and sugar. The provincial tourism site, 25 November 2024, says coconut milk, maltose, and yellow cane sugar, and names durian, peanut, cacao, and pandan as later flavors. The plain piece and the later flavors both stand.
howToEat: Eat it warm at the kiln, or take the wrapped pieces home. It is not a restaurant course.
where: The rural page places the boil at Cồn Phụng. The photograph of the wrapping table is on Cồn Quy. Town-boat kilns are the other area. No shop is named as a pick.
seoTitle: Coconut candy in Ben Tre — warm at the kiln
